programme: STAT2, CEBPG and FHL2 form a virus/damage-induced epithelial innate-immune-inflammatory module: STAT2 (part of the ISGF3-type interferon-stimulated-gene axis) drives antiviral genes (IFIT2/IFIT3, OAS1, IRF9, IRF1) alongside NF-kB-linked cytokines (IL6, CXCL8, CCL2, NFKB2); CEBPG drives the classic C/EBP-cooperating acute inflammatory programme (IL1B, NOS2, PTGS2, S100A8, CSF3); and FHL2 directly targets the NF-kB subunits RELA and NFKB1 plus the cell-cycle brake CDKN1A/CDKN1B, coupling interferon and NF-kB output to growth arrest.
role_in_a: In COPD this is a stress-response programme in airway epithelium: STAT2-driven interferon signalling is directly documented during rhinovirus-triggered exacerbations, CEBPG-driven NF-kB-cooperating inflammatory genes are seen in bronchial epithelial transcriptomes of COPD patients, and FHL2's direct targeting of RELA/NFKB1 plus CDKN1A/CDKN1B is consistent with the chronic smoke/pathogen-driven inflammation and epithelial senescence that mark the disease.
role_in_b: In lower-grade glioma no record here places STAT2, CEBPG or FHL2 specifically (Open Targets shows no association for any of the three, and no retrieved paper covers them in this disease). If the programme is real in LGG it would be expected to run in tumour cells and tumour-associated myeloid cells as part of the type-I interferon and NF-kB signalling that shapes the glioma immune microenvironment - but that is an expectation from the module's known biology, not something demonstrated in this material.
shared_axis: Both diseases involve tissue that mounts chronic interferon/NF-kB stress signalling - epithelium responding to repeated viral and pollutant insult in COPD, tumour and stromal cells responding to hypoxic/immune stress in glioma - so the same STAT2-CEBPG-FHL2 wiring could be redeployed as a generic damage-sensing module in both, without either disease being a cause of the other.
reasoning: The module is nameable and internally consistent (FHL2's direct RELA/NFKB1 targets mesh with the NF-kB-cooperating genes in CEBPG's and STAT2's target sets), and two of its three carriers are independently placed in COPD by on-topic papers (rhinovirus IFN response, bronchial epithelial RNAseq). No factor is placed in LGG by any retrieved item, so the disease-B side and the cross-disease link rest on general knowledge of interferon/NF-kB signalling in glioma rather than anything retrieved here - hence supported rather than established, and moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 31548332 - STAT2 in COPD, rhinovirus-induced TLR2/SIRT-1 regulation of type I/III interferon responses in airway epithelial cells. PMID 29506519 - CEBPG in COPD, RNAseq of bronchial epithelial cells identifying COPD-associated genes/SNPs. No paper in the material places FHL2 in either disease (its one retrieved paper concerns aortic valve stenosis).
how_to_falsify: Challenge COPD-derived airway epithelial cells and LGG-derived tumour cells (or patient organoids) in parallel with a viral mimic (poly I:C) and cigarette-smoke extract, then knock down STAT2 or CEBPG and measure induction of the shared target genes (IFIT2/OAS1 for STAT2, IL1B/PTGS2 for CEBPG) and of FHL2's direct targets RELA/NFKB1; if the glioma cells show no coupling between these three factors and NF-kB/ISG induction, the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: Brain and lung are anatomically unrelated tissues, so any concordance is not a trivial tissue-similarity artefact, but it also means no comorbidity or shared-exposure pathway is expected to corroborate it. The base is large (403 patient-group comparisons, 4 independent cohort pairs) and all three carriers recur in roughly half of them (169-214/403), which is well above the single-view cutoff. FOXP3 - a target shared by several excluded/adjacent factors (BCL11B, TRERF1, MSC) - was removed as tissue-generic, which is why a Treg/immune-checkpoint story built on those three factors was not used here: their retrieved papers were off-target (the MSC hits concern mesenchymal-stromal-cell therapy, not the musculin transcription factor; the BCL11B hit concerns sepsis-associated lung injury) or absent (TRERF1 has no retrieved paper at all). RARA, NR5A2, TCF21, MECOM, BARX2, MSC, TRERF1, CAMTA1 and BCL11B are concordant by the network-recurrence criterion but do not mechanistically join the interferon/NF-kB module and are not treated as carriers of this account.
